items.evidence: Database normalization is the systematic process of structuring relational tables to minimize data redundancy
items.note: The student clearly defines normalization and its goal of reducing data redundancy.

items.evidence: prevent anomalies like update, insert, and delete errors
items.note: The student explains that normalization prevents modification anomalies.

items.evidence: First Normal Form requires atomic values
items.note: The student states that First Normal Form requires every column to contain atomic values.
The student does not define what a functional dependency is.

items.evidence: Second and Third Normal Forms remove partial and transitive dependencies respectively
items.note: The student states that Second Normal Form eliminates partial functional dependencies.

items.evidence: Second and Third Normal Forms remove partial and transitive dependencies respectively
items.note: The student states that Third Normal Form eliminates transitive functional dependencies.

items.evidence: it often requires more joins, so designers must balance it with query performance needs
items.note: The student explains that higher normal forms can decrease read performance due to additional joins.
The student mentions balancing performance and joins, but never explicitly states denormalization as a technique to optimize read speed.

target_reason: Understanding functional dependencies is foundational for grasping how and why normal forms are structured.
target_focus: what a functional dependency is between attributes
